Team — attaching the month-end dashboard export (2026-09-dashboard-vitals.csv). A few surfaced items for leadership/QBR prep: 

- Latency: P95 for hosted API jumped from 180ms to 420ms on 9/17 for a 3-hour window; overall P50/P90 stayed steady.
- Cost: token spend normalized but infra spend per 1M tokens increased ~12% vs. Aug (GPU hours and preemption overhead).
- Uptime: 99.96% for the month, one incident on 9/17 (coincident with the latency spike) resulted in brief partial degradations; metrics in uptime-sla-meters.pdf (CC'ing infra).
- Usage: steady daily active apps but a 22% increase in long-context sessions (>4k tokens) from one partner (ACME).

Asking for: 1) a short root-cause note on the latency spike (owner: Markus?), 2) confirm cost optimization experiments status (owner: Rachel), 3) someone to pull a 2-slide QBR summary of key asks/risks for execs (owner: Laura).

Can we converge on a short readout by EOD Wed so I can fold into the QBR deck?

Adding the incident telemetry (attached uptime-sla-meters.pdf). Summary: 9/17 02:11–05:06 PT — packet-loss and elevated scheduler latencies on a mixer fleet that serves bursts for partners using long-context routing. No customer data exposure; incident was infrastructure-level and contained by autoscale and a cross-region fallback.

For QBR: recommend we call out the fallback code path as a resilience win but note a repeat-risk until the scheduler patch lands (ETA: two-week rollout). I'll drop a short blurb for the slide.

Attachments: uptime-sla-meters.pdf

— Irene
Irene Choi

Redwood Inference
From: markus.klein@redwood.com

Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sep dashboard export + highlights (attached)

Short RCA (draft): 
- Root cause: a scheduling regression in mixer v2.3.1 interacting with large batched KV-cache writes from long-context sessions (partner-facing). Under certain traffic patterns the mixer dropped high-latency tasks to reduce head-of-line blocking, which increased P95.
- Mitigation applied: rolled back mixer to v2.3.0 for affected shards (complete), added a temporary flow-control guard for KV writes.
- Next steps: schedule patch for mixer that includes better backpressure and retry semantics; target rollout window 10/05–10/07 with canary.

I attached a short diff of the trace samples and a tail of the scheduler logs (latency-spike-diff.txt). Recommend we include a 1-line risk statement in QBR: "Transient scheduling regression fixed; patch rollout planned — residual risk during canary."

Attachments: latency-spike-diff.txt

-Markus
